scope: Official-source research for post-study transitions in the Netherlands and Finland. This is research evidence, not an eligibility determination or guarantee of residence.

routes.name: Netherlands orientation year for highly educated persons
routes.summary: A non-extendable one-year permit for qualifying graduates, doctoral graduates and researchers to seek work or start a business. Eligibility depends on the specific qualifying degree/research category and its date; work is unrestricted during the permit. Staying afterwards requires a separate residence application.
routes.entryStage: Qualifying completed programme, doctorate or research; it is not an automatic consequence of any Dutch study permit.

stages.title: Complete an eligible programme or research
conditions: Within three years before application, the applicant must have completed an accredited bachelor's or master's programme at a Dutch higher education institution; a Dutch post-master's programme of at least one academic year (at least 10 months); one of the specifically listed Dutch Cultural Policy or development cooperation programmes; a master's degree in an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme; or qualifying scientific research in the Netherlands within the preceding three years.

A master's, doctoral or post-master's programme at a designated foreign educational institution can qualify. The institution must be top 200 on the date of graduation/promotion in general or subject rankings from at least two of QS, Times Higher Education or ShanghaiRanking; any subject ranking used must match the study/research subject. Foreign diplomas require Nuffic evaluation, except qualifying Flemish diplomas.

For a qualifying foreign-institution course, the applicant must also meet one of the IND's accepted language/education alternatives, including IELTS 6.0 or comparable listed test, qualifying Dutch civic-integration documents, or an English- or Dutch-taught master's, doctorate or post-master's programme.

A previous orientation-year permit after the same study/doctoral programme or same research prevents a repeat on that basis. A new Dutch programme/doctorate must be completed after the prior orientation year; qualifying research must be subsequent and held under the specified Dutch research/highly-skilled-migrant status.

The IND page lists a valid MVV as needed for the application and describes application from abroad through a Dutch representation; Dutch graduates/researchers meeting residence, valid-permit, BRP and BSN conditions can apply online. Individual nationality and general conditions can affect procedure.
stages.workRights: Not applicable as a separate post-study permit yet; student-status work rules are outside this reviewed evidence.

stages.title: Apply for the orientation-year residence permit
conditions: File within three years of the relevant graduation/promotion or research date and satisfy one of the eligibility categories above.
No income proof is required for the orientation-year application. The application fee is €254 according to IND fees page checked for the 2026 schedule.
The permit is valid for one year and cannot be extended. The IND decision period is normally up to 90 days, subject to possible extension; processing time is not an extra permit-validity period.
stages.workRights: May work freely, undertake internships, self-employment, freelancing or entrepreneurship; employer does not need a work permit. During application, work requires the qualifying evidence and an IND residence endorsement stating unrestricted work first.

stages.title: Switch to a separate work or business residence permit
conditions: A job does not automatically convert the orientation-year permit. Apply separately for a residence purpose such as highly skilled migrant, start-up or self-employed person.

For highly skilled migrant status, a Dutch employer/research institution must have an employment contract with the applicant, be an IND-recognised sponsor, and meet the salary and market-rate requirements. IND's 2026 reduced salary criterion for qualifying orientation-year graduates is €3,122 gross monthly excluding holiday pay; confirmation against the live amount table is needed at application date.
Other work/business categories have their own conditions and are not established by this route review.
stages.workRights: Work rights after the orientation year depend on the separately granted permit and its conditions; the one-year permit cannot be extended.

stages.title: Permanent residence is a separate later application
conditions: IND generally requires at least five consecutive years with a valid Dutch residence permit, main residence in the Netherlands throughout, timely extensions, continued compliance, a current non-temporary residence purpose, income, BRP registration and civic integration at least A2 (or exemption). Exceptions exist.

Do not treat the orientation-year permit itself as permanent residence or as a guarantee of eligibility. Whether particular temporary-purpose periods count in an individual case requires checking the applicable residence-credit rules and history.
stages.workRights: A permanent permit is a distinct status; this route provides no guaranteed settlement outcome.

claims.summary: Specified Dutch programme categories, Erasmus Mundus, designated foreign institutions and research can qualify; relevant completion/research must be within three years before filing. Foreign qualification has ranking, language and Nuffic assessment criteria.
Orientation-year permit lasts one year, is not extendable, and allows unrestricted employment, internship and self-employment; separate permit needed to stay for work afterward.

Orientation-year application fee €254. IND's 2026 reduced highly skilled migrant criterion is €3,122 gross monthly excluding holiday pay; route-specific eligibility and live amount must be reconfirmed when filing.

General permanent residence requirements include five consecutive years valid residence, main residence, timely extensions, current non-temporary permit, income, registration and civic integration; exceptions apply.

financialRequirements.description: 2026 IND application fee for the orientation-year permit.

2026 reduced gross salary criterion (excluding holiday pay) for a qualifying highly-skilled-migrant application linked to orientation-year eligibility; this is an employment salary threshold, not a proof-of-funds amount or fee.

unknowns: No student-admission, student-permit, tuition, insurance, dependent-cost or general relocation budget rules were reviewed; do not infer them from this post-study route.
Individual nationality, MVV exemption, general admission conditions and possible treaty-specific exceptions require case-specific checking.
Foreign-institution ranking status must be reconstructed for the exact institution, subject and graduation date; a country-level assumption is insufficient.
Eligibility and clock treatment for permanent residence depend on complete permit history and applicable law; no projected settlement date is supported.
Salary thresholds and fees are indexed/updated; recheck the official live pages at filing rather than carrying forward this snapshot.

routes.name: Finland residence permit to look for work or start a business after studies/research
routes.summary: A continuous (A) or temporary (B) permit matching the prior study/research permit type, available to eligible former permit holders after Finnish study/research completion. It can last up to two years (split into periods) and gives unrestricted work rights. Apply within five years after the study/research permit expires; separate permanent-residence rules changed on 8 January 2026.
routes.entryStage: A prior Finnish residence permit for studies or qualifying research plus degree/research completion in Finland; route-specific scope differs between EU-directive and national research permits.

stages.title: Complete studies or research in Finland while holding a qualifying permit
conditions: Applicant has or had a Finnish residence permit for studies or research and completed a degree in Finland, finished research work, or completed a doctoral degree in Finland.

For EU Directive 2016/801 research permit holders, the route may be available after Finnish degree completion or finished research. For holders of a national research permit, Migri says this route is available only if they completed a degree in Finland.
The applicant must not yet have found a job for the job-seeking application. Migri also offers the permit to start a business; business-specific requirements are not fully reviewed here.
The application may be filed already if the degree certificate will arrive within three months, with proof of expected completion, and the certificate supplied when received.
stages.workRights: Student permit work limits before grant are not covered here. This post-study permit permits unrestricted work after grant (or immediately after timely in-country extended-permit filing where Migri conditions are met).

stages.title: Apply for the look-for-work/start-business permit
conditions: Apply no later than five years from the date the study or research residence permit expired. A first residence permit application is filed abroad; an extended permit is filed in Finland. The page also states that an extended-permit application can be filed before expiry of the current permit.

Show sufficient living resources: at least €800 per month. For a full two-year permit this is €19,200 available. Migri says an extended-permit applicant may secure support through work and it checks income/benefit data through the Incomes Register.
Online fee: €750 first permit / €230 extended permit. Paper fee: €800 first permit / €430 extended permit.
stages.workRights: Unrestricted work in any field regardless of the field of study. A first-permit applicant may begin work after a positive decision. If an extended permit is submitted before prior status expires, work may begin after finding a job/starting business; a late filing does not confer that interim right.

stages.title: Use the permit continuously or in parts
conditions: Maximum total validity is two years. It can be used in up to three parts; every part must be at least six months and the last part must end within three years after the first part started.
This is a maximum permission, not an automatic grant for two years; decision, application basis and facts govern the actual permit.
stages.workRights: Unrestricted while the permit is valid.

stages.title: Move to a separate work-based permit if employment/business status is needed
conditions: Migri says the job-search permit includes unrestricted work, so a new permit is not required merely because a job is found; before the look-for-work permit expires, the applicant should apply for the appropriate work-based permit if staying on that basis. Migri identifies the degree-completed-in-Finland route for graduates with a job, trade or business activity.

The degree-completed-in-Finland permit can be sought regardless of which permit was held during study and even years after graduation; its first-permit application must be submitted abroad, while extended permits are filed in Finland.
Detailed employer, income, business and permit-validity requirements for the next work permit were not independently audited in this packet.
stages.workRights: The job-search permit already has unrestricted work rights while valid. Subsequent status depends on the new permit grant and its conditions.

stages.title: Permanent residence is a separate application with 2026 pathways
conditions: Since 8 January 2026, permanent residence rules have new application paths. Migri describes a six-year continuous A-permit residence path with two years of Finnish work history and B1 Finnish/Swedish; a four-year A-permit path with annual income over €40,000; a path for specified Finnish higher-education degrees plus developing A2 Finnish/Swedish (or 15 higher-education language credits) and other requirements; and a path involving a foreign higher degree, four years' A-permit residence and two years' Finnish work history.

For the Finnish-degree path, eligible completed qualifications include Finnish master's degrees, university bachelor's degrees, and licentiate/doctoral degrees; Migri's detailed page further states that the applicant must continue to qualify for an A permit, studies alone cannot be the basis for that A permit, and sufficient means/other requirements apply.

A person who already received a two-year continuous A permit on the job-seeking/business basis cannot receive permanent residence on the same grounds. Permanent residence is not automatic and this summary is not a computed qualifying clock.
stages.workRights: Separate permanent status; no guaranteed settlement outcome.

claims.summary: Prior Finnish study/research permit and completion of Finnish studies/degree/research required; national research-permit holders need Finnish degree completion, whereas EU research permit holders have broader scope.

claims.topic: five-year filing deadline and maximum duration
claims.summary: Apply within five years after study/research permit expiry; maximum two years, optionally in at least six-month parts, with last part ending within three years of first part start.
At least €800 monthly; two years requires €19,200. Online first/extended fees €750/€230; paper fees €800/€430.
Unrestricted work regardless of study field; work permit not needed immediately upon job if current permit valid, but apply for suitable work-based status before expiry to remain on that basis.
Finland's PR framework changed 8 January 2026 and includes work-history, income, language and Finnish-degree paths; eligibility is separate and depends on permit type and case facts.

financialRequirements.description: Minimum living resources for a look-for-work/start-business permit; not a fee, tuition amount or comprehensive budget.
Funds required to show resources for the maximum two-year period at €800 per month, as stated by Migri; not an expense estimate.

unknowns: Student admission, tuition, insurance, dependent support and study-permit financial rules were not researched in this packet; no year-one total should be calculated.
Case-specific qualification depends on exact permit class/history, degree/research type, completion date, certificate timing and where applicant files.
The separate degree-completed-in-Finland work permit's complete conditions and all variable income requirements need independent review before modelling a transition.
Permanent residence eligibility must use the post-8-Jan-2026 rules and full A/B permit chronology; do not assume student or job-search time is credited equivalently across paths.
Citizenship requirements, residence clock, language and processing were not reviewed; no citizenship or guaranteed-settlement claim is supported.
Business-start pathway details, dependants, appeal outcomes and processing-time estimate were not exhaustively verified.

notes: All facts in this file reflect direct page retrieval from issuing authorities on 2026-10-25; each page can change and should be rechecked at implementation/application time.
The routes are conditional stage transitions. A study admission or graduation is not itself a post-study permit, qualifying job, permanent residence or citizenship.
No tuition, dependent total, annual study cost or all-in first-year budget has been inferred.
